title: Anticancer potential of curcumin-cyclodextrin complexes and their pharmacokinetic properties - ScienceDirect
abstract: β-cyclodextrin has been a preferred cyclodextrin for the entrapment of curcumin due to not only its semi-natural physicochemical properties and low toxicity, but also its ability to improve drug delivery across biological membranes (Horvath et al., 2008). demonstrated that HPβCD complexes of curcumin have anti-angiogenic properties compared with the free drug, which can be beneficial for anti-cancer treatment (Yadav et al., 2009). Various studies have reported several practical techniques for increasing the aqueous solubility of curcumin, including simple heating, formation of CD complexes, and complexes in which there is no covalent binding of bovine serum albumin (BSA) to curcumin (Zhongfa et al., 2012). In a study by Zhang et al., curcumin-encapsulated chitosan-coated poly (lactic-*co*-glycolic acid) nanoparticles (CUR-CS-PLGA-NPs) and CUR-HPβCD inclusion complexes were developed and compared following intranasal administration as a possible treatment for Alzheimer’s Disease. ### Curcumin-cyclodextrin complexes enhanced the anti-cancer effects of curcumin.
